topic: Concepts of GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP in Economics
description: Various macroeconomic indicators are used to measure the national income and economic health of a country. Among these, Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross National Product (GNP), Net Domestic Product (NDP), and Net National Product (NNP) are the most crucial concepts in national income accounting.

sections.title: Basic Concepts of National Income
sections.description: Fundamental terms and definitions required to understand macroeconomic calculations.

key_concepts.explanation: The total net monetary value of all final goods and services produced by the normal residents of a country during a given financial year.
Goods that are ready for direct consumption by consumers or for capital investment. Intermediate goods are strictly excluded from national income calculations to avoid the error of 'double counting'.
The decline in the monetary value of fixed capital assets (like machinery, equipment, buildings) over time due to normal wear and tear, obsolescence, or accidental damage.

sections.title: Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
sections.description: The measure of total economic output produced within the domestic/geographical boundaries of a country.

key_concepts.explanation: The total market value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country in a specific time period (usually a financial year), regardless of whether the producers are citizens or foreign nationals.
GDP evaluated at current market prices. Since it includes the effect of inflation, an increase in Nominal GDP might just indicate rising prices rather than actual growth in production.
GDP evaluated at constant prices of a chosen 'base year'. It is adjusted for inflation and represents the true economic growth and actual increase in the production of goods and services.

scientific_principles.application: Where C = Private Consumption, I = Gross Investment, G = Government Expenditure, and (X - M) = Net Exports (Exports minus Imports).

sections.title: Gross National Product (GNP)
sections.description: The measure of total economic output produced by the citizens of a country, regardless of their location globally.

key_concepts.explanation: The total market value of all final goods and services produced by the normal residents (citizens) of a country in a year, whether the production occurs within the domestic territory or abroad.

The difference between the factor income earned by the citizens of a country from the rest of the world and the factor income earned by foreign nationals within the domestic territory of that country.

scientific_principles.application: In developing countries like India, where foreign investment is high and profits are repatriated outward, the NFIA is typically negative, making GDP greater than GNP (GDP > GNP).

sections.title: Net Domestic Product & Net National Product
sections.description: The 'Net' macroeconomic aggregates obtained by subtracting capital depreciation from the gross figures.

key_concepts.explanation: The value obtained by subtracting the depreciation of capital assets from the Gross Domestic Product (GDP). It is always lower than the GDP and reflects the net domestic output.
The value obtained by subtracting depreciation from the Gross National Product (GNP). Specifically, 'NNP at Factor Cost' is officially considered the true 'National Income' of a country.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: NDP = GDP - Depreciation | NNP = GNP - Depreciation
scientific_principles.application: These formulas are used to measure the real net growth and the true retained productive capacity of an economy after accounting for capital wear and tear.

sections.title: Important Concepts and Facts
sections.description: Crucial distinctions between Market Price and Factor Cost, along with high-yield exam facts related to National Income.

key_concepts.explanation: The total cost of all factors of production (land, labor, capital, entrepreneurship) used in producing goods and services. It represents the actual cost of production, excluding any government taxes.
The final retail price at which goods and services are actually sold to consumers in the open market. (Market Price = Factor Cost + Indirect Taxes - Subsidies).

important_facts.fact: The current Base Year used for calculating National Income and GDP series in India is 2011-12.
Dadabhai Naoroji was the first person to scientifically estimate India's National Income and Per Capita Income in 1867-68, as detailed in his famous book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

Per Capita Income (PCI) is calculated by dividing a country's Total National Income by its Total Population, serving as the most reliable indicator of the average standard of living and economic well-being.
